bug_semantics: Scriban enforced TemplateContext.LoopLimit only when script-level for/while loops called StepLoop. A single attacker-controlled expression could instead perform expensive internal iteration without StepLoop: a lazy 1..N range yielded N values and array.size exhausted a non-ICollection with LINQ Count(), while string * int appended in an ordinary for loop. ScriptBlockStatement checked cancellation only once around the whole statement, so these internal loops could consume excessive CPU or memory before another abort check. Applications rendering untrusted templates that treated a small LoopLimit as an execution bound were therefore exposed to denial of service.
flaw_origin: The earliest public source commit, 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 (Initial version), introduced the flawed design atomically: src/Textamina.Scriban/TemplateOptions.cs created LoopLimit with a default of 1000; src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/ScriptBinaryExpression.cs implemented range generators as unchecked yield loops; and src/Textamina.Scriban/Helpers/ArrayFunctions.cs implemented Size(IEnumerable) by exhausting non-collections with list.Cast<object>().Count(), with other built-ins likewise iterating without TemplateContext. History searches show that exact Size slow path and the original RangeInclude implementation first appear in this root commit. Later namespace moves/reorganizations, including 19867811c2bbd3a438e188b85ea370da946ad06e, merely moved existing flawed lines and are not BICs. The later string-multiplication amplification path was added by 4175ec0cd75adcc459810abbf9e3e0a9d360ffb3, but the independently exploitable range/array.size LoopLimit bypass already existed at the root commit, making the root commit the smallest BIC for the advisory mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object (git cat-file -p 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589) names author Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, has the message exactly 'Initial version', contains no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and has no bot identity or any other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-c875-h985-hvrc states that ScriptBlockStatement checks abort once per statement, LoopLimit is tied to script-loop StepLoop, array.size at src/Scriban/Functions/ArrayFunctions.cs exhausts non-collection enumerables, ranges in src/Scriban/Syntax/Expressions/ScriptBinaryExpression.cs / src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptRange.cs yield without StepLoop, and string multiplication loops without the limit; it declares NuGet scriban <= 6.6.0 affected and 7.0.0 patched. The assigned global advisory is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5vwr-vwx4-9hc3 (CVE-2026-74789). BIC: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589. `git log 6.6.0 --reverse -S'return list.Cast<object>().Count();' --all -- src` and the corresponding -S search for `private static IEnumerable<int> RangeInclude` both lead to 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589. Its tree has src/Textamina.Scriban/Helpers/ArrayFunctions.cs:50-60 (unchecked Size slow path), src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/ScriptBinaryExpression.cs:155-199 (unchecked inclusive/exclusive yield loops), and src/Textamina.Scriban/TemplateOptions.cs:16-30 (LoopLimit). Parent/absence verification: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589` returns only that SHA and `git cat-file -p` has no parent line, proving it is the repository root; `git diff-tree --root --name-status` reports all three vulnerable source files as A, so the vulnerable lines are absent from the empty pre-root tree. There is therefore no 40-hex parent commit to report, rather than an unexamined parent. The root snapshot is a normal root commit, not a marked squash or merge, and no member commits exist to decompose. The string-amplification loop first appears later in 4175ec0cd75adcc459810abbf9e3e0a9d360ffb3, but does not displace the earlier range/size BIC. Fix: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9 adds context-aware built-in overloads and calls context.StepLoop(span, ref loopStep, loopType) while enumerating Size and the other internal iteration paths; this is the smallest direct fix for the advisory's central built-in-iteration defect. Its immediate companion https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/2d01bd15a1114fac2533aa005036e07389ee89db validates range size against LoopLimit and string multiplication against LimitToString. Boundary checks: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proves the BIC is in tag 6.6.0 (tag target b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7) and even v0.1.0, proves dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9 is not in 6.6.0, and proves it is in 7.0.0 (tag target 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f), matching https://github.com/scriban/scriban/releases/tag/6.6.0 and https://github.com/scriban/scriban/releases/tag/7.0.0 and the advisory's <=6.6.0 / 7.0.0 boundary.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that a large range or string can be requested; it is the mismatch between LoopLimit's safety role and the execution architecture. Script-loop statements debit StepLoop, but expression operators and built-ins performed their own iteration with no TemplateContext accounting, allowing one statement to do work proportional to attacker-selected N. The public history establishes that this mismatch was present from the first source snapshot: the same root commit created LoopLimit, the lazy range loops, and the Size slow path. A later namespace rename and subsequent refactors preserve rather than introduce it, and the 2020 string-multiplication addition is an additional attack path, not the earliest cause. Because the BIC is a root commit, there is no immediate parent commit SHA; the no-parent commit object plus root diff against the empty tree is the strongest possible parent-absence verification and shows the vulnerable files/lines were created there. The March 2026 fix sequence first bounded ranges/string growth in 2d01bd15a1114fac2533aa005036e07389ee89db and then directly repaired the general missing-accounting mechanism in dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9 by passing context into built-ins and debiting each internal iteration. The final direct fix is absent from affected 6.6.0 and present in patched 7.0.0. Finally, the only attribution evidence considered is the exact BIC commit object: it is authored and committed by Alexandre Mutel and has no AI/bot marker or trailer. AI attribution on any later commit, including fixes, is causally irrelevant under the protocol; therefore the result is NOT_AI.
